strings.ext.intro: Brave Shields is already a native ad and tracker blocker (same filter-list lineage as uBlock Origin, but built in, so slightly faster). Nothing is force-installed - that would show a "Managed by your organization" banner and lock the extension on. These buttons just open the install pages in Brave.
strings.ext.warn: Caution: uBlock Origin on top of Shields blocks the same things twice, wastes CPU per tab and can break sites Shields handles fine. If you add it, set Shields to Standard rather than Aggressive.
strings.filter.help: Search every setting: a name, a word from its description, a policy name...

strings.header.compat.older: Your Brave (version {0}) is much older than the one this list was checked against ({1}). Some settings may not exist yet in your version and will simply be ignored.
strings.header.help: How this works, what each status means, and how to undo
strings.header.policiesShared: Policies apply to every Brave channel on this PC (Stable, Beta, Nightly and Dev share one policy location).
strings.header.subtitle: Turn off the extras you do not want in Brave. Every change is reversible.
strings.help.compat.body:
This list of settings was checked against Brave {0} (Chromium {1}) on {2}. Brave changes its policies over time, so on a newer Brave a few settings may be renamed or gone, and on an older one some may not exist yet. Brave simply ignores policies it does not know, so nothing breaks - open brave://policy to see which ones your version accepts.

Your Brave: {3}. Everything this app does is reversible.
strings.help.compat.title: Brave versions
strings.help.footer: Brave Free Origin v{0}  -  {1}  -  log file: {2}
strings.help.managed.body: Brave shows this whenever any machine policy is active. It is a Chromium transparency feature and cannot be hidden safely. It disappears when you remove the policies (Stock / None, then Apply, or Restore stock).
strings.help.managed.title: The "Managed by your organization" note
strings.help.status.body:
Active: already applied.
Will apply, Will change, Will remove: waiting for you to press Apply.
Not set: Brave decides.
Set elsewhere, Will replace: something else (your organization, another tool) already set a different value. Apply shows it to you first and only replaces it if you agree.

Risk says what you could lose. Safe and Low are fine for everyone; Medium and High change how Brave behaves, so read the description first. Rows marked as locks only make Brave's own default mandatory.
strings.help.status.title: What the Status and Risk columns mean
strings.help.tick.body: Tick a setting to make this app enforce it. Untick it to hand control back to Brave: the policy is removed when you press Apply. Nothing is written until you press Apply, and Preview changes shows exactly what would happen first.
strings.help.tick.title: Ticking a setting
strings.help.title: How Brave Free Origin works
strings.help.undo.title: Undoing everything
strings.help.what.body: Brave Free Origin switches off Brave features you do not want. It uses Brave's official group policies - the same mechanism companies use to manage browsers - written to the Windows registry. It never modifies Brave's program files (only the optional expert Scriptlets page edits filter-list files, and only when you ask, with a backup), and it works for every Brave channel installed on this PC.
strings.help.what.title: What this app does
strings.hosts.ads.description: Servers for Brave Ads. Block them only if Rewards is switched off - Ads stop working if you turn Rewards back on.
strings.hosts.ads.name: Brave Ads servers
strings.hosts.components.description: The servers Brave's Shields filter lists, extensions and Tor come from. Blocking them freezes ad blocking, Widevine and extension updates. Experts only - never needed for privacy.
strings.hosts.components.name: Component and extension updates
strings.hosts.crash.description: The server that receives Brave crash reports. Reports are only sent if you agreed to them; blocking it is a safety net.
strings.hosts.crash.name: Brave crash reports
strings.hosts.news.description: The servers behind the News feed and its images. Block them only if News is switched off - it stops working if you turn it back on.
strings.hosts.news.name: Brave News servers
strings.hosts.p3a.description: The servers that receive Brave's anonymous usage analytics (P3A). Pure telemetry, never needed by a feature.
strings.hosts.p3a.name: Brave usage analytics (P3A)
strings.hosts.rewards.description: Servers for Brave Rewards. Block them only if you do not use Rewards - it stops working if you turn it back on.
strings.hosts.rewards.name: Brave Rewards servers
strings.hosts.stats.description: The server behind Brave's anonymous daily usage ping. Pure telemetry.
strings.hosts.stats.name: Brave usage ping
strings.hosts.variations.description: The server that sends Brave remote experiments and kill switches. Matches the Max Privacy setting that turns experiments off.
strings.hosts.variations.name: Brave experiments (Variations)
strings.hosts.webDiscovery.description: Servers for the Web Discovery Project. It is opt-in and off by default; blocking them is a safety net.
strings.hosts.webDiscovery.name: Web Discovery Project
strings.hostsTab.warn: Independent of the Apply to Brave button: use the buttons below to write or remove the hosts block. Only the Brave Free Origin block is edited; a backup is saved first.
strings.log.updater.missing: That updater item is not installed on this PC, so there is nothing to change.
strings.msg.apply.allKept: Nothing was changed. You chose to keep every existing setting as it is.
strings.msg.apply.nothing: There is nothing to change. Tick or untick settings first, or pick a preset.

This restores stock Brave.

It removes the policies this tool set, clears the Brave-Free-Origin hosts block and turns Brave's updater tasks and services back on if they are disabled.

Continue?

No: remove everything, including those {0}

strings.page.aiGenAi.intro: Brave's own AI plus the Google-based AI features that ship with Chromium. Ticking keeps them off.
strings.page.aiGenAi.title: AI features
strings.page.autofillPasswords.intro: Convenience features that store personal data. Turning them off is stricter, but less convenient.
strings.page.autofillPasswords.title: Passwords and autofill
strings.page.braveFeatures.intro: Features Brave adds on top of the browser. Tick one to switch it off for good.
strings.page.braveFeatures.title: Brave extras
strings.page.hosts.intro: A second line of defence: block Brave's telemetry domains at the Windows level. This page has its own Apply button and never runs from the main one.
strings.page.hosts.title: Hosts blocklist
strings.page.overrides.intro: Choose the address-bar search engine and what opens on launch and on new tabs. Each section only applies when its box is ticked.
strings.page.overrides.title: Search engine and startup
strings.page.performanceStartup.intro: Memory, battery, disk and what opens when Brave starts.
strings.page.performanceStartup.title: Performance and startup
strings.page.privacyTelemetry.intro: Usage statistics, crash reports and remote experiments. Ticking stops the data from being sent.
strings.page.privacyTelemetry.title: Telemetry and reports
strings.page.safetyUpdates.intro: Safe Browsing details and the prompts Brave shows about itself.
strings.page.safetyUpdates.title: Safety and prompts
strings.page.scriptlets.intro: Optional expert tool: view Brave's built-in adblock scriptlet rules from component filter lists. Editing is manual-only, never part of presets, and never triggered by Apply to Brave.
strings.page.scriptlets.title: Scriptlets (expert)
strings.page.searchSuggestions.intro: What the address bar and text boxes send to web services while you type.
strings.page.searchSuggestions.title: Search and suggestions
strings.page.shieldsProtection.intro: Brave's built-in tracking protection. Most of it is already on; ticking locks it so nothing can weaken it later.
strings.page.shieldsProtection.title: Shields and tracking
strings.page.signinImport.intro: Account, sync and first-run import features. Mostly for people who want a strictly local browser.
strings.page.signinImport.title: Sign-in, sync and import
strings.page.sitePermissions.intro: Decide for every site at once instead of being asked. Ticking blocks the permission by default; sites that need it stop working.
strings.page.sitePermissions.title: Site permissions
strings.page.uiBloatExtras.intro: Small interface features you can remove.
strings.page.uiBloatExtras.title: Interface clutter
strings.page.updater.intro: Advanced. Only for people who update Brave by hand. Presets never change this page.
strings.page.updater.title: Updater tasks and services
strings.page.webServicesBackground.intro: What Brave does in the background and on the network.
strings.page.webServicesBackground.title: Network and background
strings.policy.AIModeSettings.description: Blocks Google's AI Mode shortcuts in the address bar and New Tab search box. Only relevant when Google is your search engine.
strings.policy.AIModeSettings.title: Turn off Google AI Mode shortcuts
strings.policy.AccessibilityImageLabelsEnabled.d: For screen-reader users: stops unlabeled images from being sent to a Google service to get automatic descriptions. Screen-reader users lose those descriptions.
strings.policy.AlternateErrorPagesEnabled.descri: Stops asking a web service for suggestions when a page cannot be found. Brave already has this off; ticking locks it.
strings.policy.AlternateErrorPagesEnabled.title: Turn off error-page suggestions
strings.policy.AutofillAddressEnabled.descriptio: Brave stops suggesting, saving and filling addresses and contact details. Entries you already saved are kept but no longer offered.
strings.policy.AutofillAddressEnabled.title: Turn off address autofill
strings.policy.AutofillCreditCardEnabled.descrip: Brave stops suggesting, saving and filling payment cards, so you type card numbers by hand.
strings.policy.AutofillCreditCardEnabled.title: Turn off card autofill
strings.policy.AutofillPredictionSettings.descri: Stops Chromium from using generative AI to understand forms and fill more fields.
strings.policy.AutofillPredictionSettings.title: Turn off AI-enhanced autofill
strings.policy.AutoplayAllowed.description: Stops videos and audio from starting on their own. Sites need a click to play, so some previews and players wait for you.
strings.policy.AutoplayAllowed.title: Block media autoplay
strings.policy.BackgroundModeEnabled.description: Stops Brave from staying alive in the system tray after you close the last window, which would keep extensions and notifications running.
strings.policy.BackgroundModeEnabled.title: Do not run Brave in the background
strings.policy.BatterySaverModeAvailability.desc: Reduces animations and background work when a laptop is unplugged and the battery is low. Users cannot turn Battery Saver off.
strings.policy.BatterySaverModeAvailability.titl: Use Battery Saver on low battery
strings.policy.BlockExternalExtensions.descripti: Stops other programs on this PC from adding browser extensions to Brave behind your back (through the registry or extension files). Apps that bundle a companion extension can no longer install it on their own - add it from the store instead.
strings.policy.BlockExternalExtensions.title: Block extensions added by other programs
strings.policy.BookmarkBarEnabled.description: Hides the bookmarks bar under the address bar, and it cannot be shown again in Settings.
strings.policy.BookmarkBarEnabled.title: Hide the bookmarks bar
strings.policy.BraveAIChatEnabled.description: Removes Leo, Brave's built-in AI chat, from the sidebar, the address bar and the right-click menu.
strings.policy.BraveAIChatEnabled.title: Turn off Leo AI assistant
strings.policy.BraveDeAmpEnabled.description: Opens the publisher's real page instead of Google's AMP copy, which limits tracking. Brave does this by default; ticking locks it on.
strings.policy.BraveDeAmpEnabled.title: Skip Google AMP pages
strings.policy.BraveDebouncingEnabled.descriptio: Sends you straight to your destination when a link goes through a known tracking redirect. On by default; ticking locks it on. Rarely, a redirect-based login can behave differently.
strings.policy.BraveDebouncingEnabled.title: Skip tracker redirects
Tells websites you do not want your data sold or shared (Global Privacy Control). On by default; ticking locks it on.
strings.policy.BraveLocalAIEnabled.description: Hides Brave's on-device AI features (such as history embeddings) and stops the AI model component from being installed.
strings.policy.BraveLocalAIEnabled.title: Turn off Brave's on-device AI
strings.policy.BraveNewsDisabled.description: Removes the news feed from the New Tab page and its related settings.
strings.policy.BraveNewsDisabled.title: Turn off Brave News
strings.policy.BraveP3AEnabled.description: P3A sends anonymous, privacy-preserving answers about how Brave features are used. Ticking turns it off and it cannot be switched back on in Settings.
strings.policy.BraveP3AEnabled.title: Turn off usage analytics (P3A)
strings.policy.BravePlaylistEnabled.description: Removes Playlist, which saves videos and audio from web pages so you can play them later or offline.
strings.policy.BravePlaylistEnabled.title: Turn off Playlist
strings.policy.BraveReduceLanguageEnabled.descri: Limits what sites can learn from your language settings, which makes fingerprinting harder. On by default; ticking locks it on. A few multilingual sites may pick a default language.
strings.policy.BraveReduceLanguageEnabled.title: Hide language details from sites
strings.policy.BraveRewardsDisabled.description: Removes Brave Rewards (BAT tokens for viewing ads), its ads, tips and buttons. It cannot be switched back on in Settings.
strings.policy.BraveRewardsDisabled.title: Turn off Brave Rewards
strings.policy.BraveSpeedreaderEnabled.descripti: Removes the reading-mode button that turns cluttered articles into a clean view.
strings.policy.BraveSpeedreaderEnabled.title: Turn off Speedreader
strings.policy.BraveStatsPingEnabled.description: Stops the small daily ping that lets Brave count active users.
strings.policy.BraveStatsPingEnabled.title: Turn off the usage ping
strings.policy.BraveTalkDisabled.description: Removes the Brave Talk video-call button and its promotions from the browser.
strings.policy.BraveTalkDisabled.title: Turn off Brave Talk
strings.policy.BraveTrackingQueryParametersFilte: Removes known tracking codes (such as fbclid) from links when Shields is on. On by default; ticking locks it on. Rarely, a link that needs such a code stops working.
strings.policy.BraveVPNDisabled.description: Removes the paid Brave VPN button, menu entries and upsell. Other VPNs are not affected.
strings.policy.BraveVPNDisabled.title: Turn off Brave VPN
strings.policy.BraveWalletDisabled.description: Removes the built-in crypto wallet (Ethereum, Solana, Bitcoin and more), its toolbar button and Web3 features such as .eth and .sol addresses.
strings.policy.BraveWalletDisabled.title: Turn off Brave Wallet
strings.policy.BraveWaybackMachineEnabled.descri: Stops Brave from offering an archived copy from the Internet Archive when a page is missing, and hides its icon and settings.
strings.policy.BraveWaybackMachineEnabled.title: Turn off Wayback Machine prompts
strings.policy.BraveWebDiscoveryEnabled.descript: The Web Discovery Project anonymously shares data to help build Brave Search. It is opt-in and off by default; ticking makes sure it stays off.
strings.policy.BraveWebDiscoveryEnabled.title: Keep Web Discovery off
strings.policy.BrowserLabsEnabled.description: Hides the Labs (experiments) button from the toolbar. Brave already does not show it; ticking locks it.
strings.policy.BrowserLabsEnabled.title: Hide the Labs button
strings.policy.BrowserSignin.description: Prevents signing in to the browser with an account. Brave has no Google-account sign-in, so this is mostly a safety lock.
strings.policy.BrowserSignin.title: Block browser sign-in
strings.policy.BuiltInDnsClientEnabled.descripti: Makes Brave ask Windows for DNS lookups instead of using its own DNS client. The built-in client is still used when secure DNS is on.
strings.policy.BuiltInDnsClientEnabled.title: Use Windows for DNS lookups
strings.policy.ChromeVariations.description: Variations let Brave switch features on or off remotely (experiments, staged rollouts, kill switches). Ticking blocks all of them, so you only get built-in defaults - which can delay remote fixes.
strings.policy.ChromeVariations.title: Turn off remote experiments
strings.policy.ComponentUpdatesEnabled.descripti: Stops Brave from updating its internal components (such as Widevine, and probably ad-block filter lists) between browser releases. Streaming and blocking data can go stale or break. Experts only.
strings.policy.ComponentUpdatesEnabled.title: Stop background component updates
strings.policy.CreateThemesSettings.description: Blocks the feature that generates custom themes and wallpapers with AI.
strings.policy.CreateThemesSettings.title: Turn off AI-generated themes
strings.policy.DNSInterceptionChecksEnabled.desc: Brave normally sends a few test DNS lookups at startup and when your network changes, to spot ISPs that redirect unknown names. Ticking skips them. On such networks, a single word typed in the address bar may act oddly.
strings.policy.DNSInterceptionChecksEnabled.titl: Skip the DNS hijack test at startup
strings.policy.DefaultBraveAdblockSetting.descri: Sets Shields' default to "Block ads and trackers" and stops the global default being changed to "Allow". Brave already blocks by default; ticking locks it.
strings.policy.DefaultBraveAdblockSetting.title: Keep ad blocking on
strings.policy.DefaultBraveFingerprintingV2Setti: Locks fingerprinting protection to Standard, which makes it harder for sites to recognise your browser by its unique traits. Brave's default; a few captchas and web apps may misbehave.
strings.policy.DefaultBraveHttpsUpgradeSetting.d: Upgrades every link to HTTPS and shows a warning page instead of opening a site that has no HTTPS. Old routers, NAS boxes and local http:// pages need extra clicks or will not open.
strings.policy.DefaultBraveReferrersSetting.desc: Limits the "Referer" header to your site's origin for cross-site requests, so other sites do not see the full address you came from. Brave does this by default; ticking locks it.
strings.policy.DefaultBraveReferrersSetting.titl: Limit the referrer sent to sites
strings.policy.DefaultBraveRemember1PStorageSett: Deletes a site's cookies and storage when you close its tab, so you are signed out of sites all the time and lose saved site settings. Brave normally keeps them.
Forget site data when a tab closes
strings.policy.DefaultBrowserSettingEnabled.desc: Stops Brave from checking whether it is your default browser and asking you to change it. Set your default in Windows Settings instead.
strings.policy.DefaultIdleDetectionSetting.descr: Sites can ask to know when you step away from the computer. Ticking answers "no" for every site without asking. Chat and team apps can no longer show an automatic "away" status.
strings.policy.DefaultIdleDetectionSetting.title: Block sites from seeing when you are idle
strings.policy.DefaultLocalFontsSetting.descript: Your installed fonts are a fingerprinting signal. Ticking stops sites from asking to see them. Online design tools cannot use your installed fonts.
strings.policy.DefaultLocalFontsSetting.title: Block sites from listing your fonts
strings.policy.DefaultSensorsSetting.description: Sites can read device motion, orientation and light sensors, which helps them fingerprint you. Ticking denies that by default. Some maps, 360 viewers and web games that react to tilt stop responding to motion.
strings.policy.DefaultSensorsSetting.title: Block sites from reading motion sensors
strings.policy.DefaultSerialGuardSetting.descrip: Websites can normally ask to open serial (COM) ports, for 3D printers or microcontrollers. Ticking answers "no" without asking. Web serial consoles and hardware flashers stop working.
strings.policy.DefaultSerialGuardSetting.title: Block sites from using serial ports
strings.policy.DefaultWebBluetoothGuardSetting.d: Websites can normally ask to connect to nearby Bluetooth gadgets. Ticking answers "no" without asking. Web tools for Bluetooth hardware stop working; regular Windows Bluetooth (headphones, mice) is not affected.
strings.policy.DefaultWebBluetoothGuardSetting.t: Block sites from using Bluetooth devices
strings.policy.DefaultWebHidGuardSetting.descrip: Websites can normally ask to talk to game controllers, keyboards and macro pads directly. Ticking answers "no" without asking. Web configurators for such devices stop working.
strings.policy.DefaultWebHidGuardSetting.title: Block sites from using HID input devices
strings.policy.DefaultWebUsbGuardSetting.descrip: Websites can normally ask to talk to USB gadgets. Ticking answers "no" without asking. Web tools that flash or configure USB hardware stop working.
strings.policy.DefaultWebUsbGuardSetting.title: Block sites from using USB devices
strings.policy.DefaultWindowManagementSetting.de: Sites can ask about your screens and place windows across them. Ticking answers "no" without asking. Presentation and multi-monitor web apps lose that ability.
strings.policy.DefaultWindowManagementSetting.ti: Block sites from seeing your monitors
strings.policy.DesktopSharingHubEnabled.descript: Removes the Share menu from the address bar and the page right-click menu.
strings.policy.DesktopSharingHubEnabled.title: Remove the Share button
strings.policy.DevToolsGenAiSettings.description: DevTools' Console Insights and AI assistance send errors, code and network details to a Google AI model. Ticking turns them off; developers lose the AI hints.
strings.policy.DevToolsGenAiSettings.title: Turn off AI helpers in DevTools
strings.policy.DiskCacheSize.description: Caps how much disk space the page cache may use (250 MB). The limit is a hint, not exact, and heavy browsing re-downloads more files.
strings.policy.DiskCacheSize.title: Limit the disk cache to 250 MB
strings.policy.DnsOverHttpsMode.description: Encrypts DNS lookups (DNS-over-HTTPS) when your provider supports it, and falls back to normal DNS if not. You cannot switch it off or pick a custom provider.
strings.policy.DnsOverHttpsMode.title: Use secure DNS when available
strings.policy.EmailAliasesEnabled.description: Removes Email Aliases, the feature that creates disposable addresses for sign-ups, together with its buttons.
strings.policy.EmailAliasesEnabled.title: Turn off Email Aliases
strings.policy.EnableMediaRouter.description: Removes Google Cast (sending tabs to TVs and speakers) and stops Brave scanning your network for Cast devices.
strings.policy.EnableMediaRouter.title: Turn off Google Cast
strings.policy.GeminiSettings.description: Blocks the Gemini app integration in the browser.
strings.policy.GeminiSettings.title: Turn off Gemini integration
strings.policy.GenAILocalFoundationalModelSettin: Stops Chromium's large on-device AI model from being downloaded, and deletes it if it is already there.
Do not download the on-device AI model
strings.policy.HardwareAccelerationModeEnabled.d: Lets Brave use your graphics card to draw pages and decode video. On is Brave's default. Pick Off only to work around GPU driver glitches, artifacts or crashes - video and scrolling get slower.
strings.policy.HelpMeWriteSettings.description: Blocks "Help me write", Google's AI writing helper for text boxes on the web.
strings.policy.HelpMeWriteSettings.title: Turn off "Help me write"
strings.policy.HighEfficiencyModeEnabled.descrip: Puts tabs you have not used for a while to sleep so their memory can be reused. They reload when you return to them.
strings.policy.HighEfficiencyModeEnabled.title: Turn on Memory Saver
strings.policy.HistorySearchSettings.description: Blocks Google's AI history search, which answers questions using the content of pages in your history.
strings.policy.HistorySearchSettings.title: Turn off AI history search
strings.policy.HomepageIsNewTabPage.description: Separates the Home page from the New Tab page, so the Home button opens its own address. Only matters when the Home button is shown.
strings.policy.HomepageIsNewTabPage.title: Home page is not the New Tab page
strings.policy.HomepageLocation.description: Makes the Home button open a blank page and stops it being changed.
strings.policy.HomepageLocation.title: Set the Home page to blank
strings.policy.ImportAutofillFormData.descriptio: Stops form-autofill data from being imported from your previous browser on first run; the import box starts unticked.
strings.policy.ImportAutofillFormData.title: Do not import form data
strings.policy.ImportBookmarks.description: Stops bookmarks from being imported from your previous browser on first run; the import box starts unticked.
strings.policy.ImportBookmarks.title: Do not import bookmarks
strings.policy.ImportHistory.description: Stops browsing history from being imported from your previous browser on first run; the import box starts unticked.
strings.policy.ImportHistory.title: Do not import history
strings.policy.ImportSavedPasswords.description: Blocks importing saved passwords from another browser, on first run and also manually from Settings.
strings.policy.ImportSavedPasswords.title: Block importing saved passwords
strings.policy.ImportSearchEngine.description: Stops the search engine from being imported from your previous browser on first run; the import box starts unticked.
strings.policy.ImportSearchEngine.title: Do not import search engines
strings.policy.LiveCaptionEnabled.description: Turns off Live Caption, which creates on-device captions for audio and video and needs a speech-model download. Deaf and hard-of-hearing users lose automatic captions.
strings.policy.LiveCaptionEnabled.title: Turn off Live Caption
strings.policy.MetricsReportingEnabled.descripti: Stops Chromium's usage statistics and crash reports from being sent. Brave then gets no crash data from you, which can slow down bug fixes.
strings.policy.MetricsReportingEnabled.title: Turn off crash and usage reports
strings.policy.NTPCustomBackgroundEnabled.descri: Users can no longer set their own New Tab background, and a custom background already set is permanently deleted - removing this policy later does not bring it back.
strings.policy.NTPCustomBackgroundEnabled.title: Block custom New Tab backgrounds
strings.policy.NetworkPredictionOptions.descript: Stops DNS prefetching, pre-connecting and pre-rendering of pages the browser guesses you will open. Brave already has this off; ticking locks it. Some pages may load slightly slower.
strings.policy.NetworkPredictionOptions.title: Turn off page preloading
strings.policy.NewTabPageLocation.description: Every new tab opens an empty page instead of Brave's New Tab page (top sites, background, News). No favorites or search box on new tabs.
strings.policy.NewTabPageLocation.title: Make new tabs blank
strings.policy.PasswordLeakDetectionEnabled.desc: Stops the breach check that sends a hashed copy of credentials to a Google service. Brave already has it off; ticking locks it off.
strings.policy.PasswordManagerEnabled.descriptio: Brave stops asking to save new passwords. Passwords you already saved still fill in. You will need another password manager for new logins.
strings.policy.PasswordManagerEnabled.title: Stop offering to save passwords
strings.policy.PaymentMethodQueryEnabled.descrip: Stops websites from checking (through the Payment Request API) whether you have a saved payment method. Some checkouts lose their one-click card option.
strings.policy.PaymentMethodQueryEnabled.title: Hide saved cards from websites
strings.policy.PromotionsEnabled.description: Stops Brave from opening full-tab promotional content and welcome pages.
strings.policy.PromotionsEnabled.title: Hide promo and welcome tabs
strings.policy.PromptForDownloadLocation.descrip: Downloads start at once into your Downloads folder instead of asking where to save each file. Unwanted downloads are less obvious.
strings.policy.PromptForDownloadLocation.title: Save downloads without asking
strings.policy.PsstEnabled.description: Stops Brave from suggesting and adjusting site-specific privacy settings on its own.
strings.policy.PsstEnabled.title: Turn off Privacy Settings Tuning
strings.policy.QRCodeGeneratorEnabled.descriptio: Removes "Create QR code for this page" from the address bar and the right-click menu.
strings.policy.QRCodeGeneratorEnabled.title: Remove "Create QR code"
strings.policy.QuicAllowed.description: Allows QUIC, the faster HTTP/3 web protocol. It is allowed by default, so ticking only locks it on. A few corporate firewalls block QUIC.
strings.policy.QuicAllowed.title: Always allow QUIC (HTTP/3)
strings.policy.RestoreOnStartup.description: Brave normally continues where you left off. Ticking makes it always open the New Tab page instead, and you lose your tabs after a restart or crash.
strings.policy.RestoreOnStartup.title: Start on the New Tab page
strings.policy.SafeBrowsingDeepScanningEnabled.d: Stops suspicious downloads from being uploaded to Google for a malware scan. Brave already has this off; ticking locks it.
strings.policy.SafeBrowsingExtendedReportingEnab: Stops sending system information and page content to Google when a threat is detected. Brave already has this off; ticking locks it.
Never send extra Safe Browsing reports
strings.policy.SafeBrowsingProtectionLevel.descr: Keeps Safe Browsing (dangerous-site and download warnings) on Standard and blocks "Enhanced" (shares more data with Google) and "Off".
strings.policy.SafeBrowsingProtectionLevel.title: Keep Safe Browsing on Standard
strings.policy.SafeBrowsingSurveysEnabled.descri: Prevents Safe Browsing satisfaction surveys from appearing.
strings.policy.SafeBrowsingSurveysEnabled.title: Stop Safe Browsing surveys
strings.policy.SearchContentSharingSettings.desc: Stops the browser from sharing page or file content with Google AI Mode and Lens. This one policy replaces the older Lens policies.
strings.policy.SearchContentSharingSettings.titl: Stop sharing page content with Google AI
strings.policy.SearchSuggestEnabled.description: Stops the address bar from sending what you type to your search engine to fetch suggestions. Brave already has this off; ticking locks it. History and bookmark suggestions still work.
strings.policy.SearchSuggestEnabled.title: Turn off search suggestions
strings.policy.ShowHomeButton.description: Removes the Home button from the toolbar. Brave hides it by default; ticking locks it hidden.
strings.policy.ShowHomeButton.title: Hide the Home button
strings.policy.SpellCheckServiceEnabled.descript: Stops sending the text you type to a Google web service for smarter spell checking. Local spell checking keeps working.
strings.policy.SpellCheckServiceEnabled.title: Turn off cloud spellcheck
strings.policy.SpellcheckEnabled.description: Disables all spell checking, local and cloud. No red underlines or suggestions anywhere, and it cannot be turned back on in Settings.
strings.policy.SpellcheckEnabled.title: Turn off spellcheck completely
strings.policy.SyncDisabled.description: Turns off syncing of bookmarks, passwords, history and settings between your devices, and it cannot be turned back on in Settings.
strings.policy.SyncDisabled.title: Turn off Brave Sync
strings.policy.TabCompareSettings.description: Blocks the AI tool that compares information across your open tabs.
strings.policy.TabCompareSettings.title: Turn off AI tab comparison
strings.policy.ThirdPartyAiChatSettings.descript: Blocks AI chat shortcuts from third-party search engines in the address bar and New Tab search box.
strings.policy.ThirdPartyAiChatSettings.title: Turn off third-party AI chat shortcuts
strings.policy.TorDisabled.description: Removes "New Private Window with Tor". Tor inside Brave is weaker than the official Tor Browser, so you may not miss it.
strings.policy.TorDisabled.title: Turn off Tor private windows
strings.policy.TranslateEnabled.description: Removes Brave's built-in "Translate this page" offer. Pages in other languages stay untranslated.
strings.policy.TranslateEnabled.title: Turn off page translation
strings.policy.UrlKeyedAnonymizedDataCollectionE: Prevents the addresses of pages you visit from being sent to Google to "make searches and browsing better". It is opt-in; ticking makes sure it cannot be enabled.
strings.policy.UserFeedbackAllowed.description: Removes the "Send feedback" option that can attach diagnostics to a report.
strings.policy.UserFeedbackAllowed.title: Turn off "Send feedback"
strings.policy.WebRtcEventLogCollectionAllowed.d: Stops services such as Google Meet from collecting WebRTC diagnostic logs from your browser. Brave already blocks this; ticking locks it.
strings.policy.WebRtcIPHandling.description: Websites can normally learn your device's local network address through WebRTC. Ticking limits WebRTC to your public address only, which some video-call and peer-to-peer sites do not like.
strings.policy.WebRtcIPHandling.title: Hide your local network address (WebRTC)
strings.preset.CurrentState.description: What is set on this PC right now. Pick a preset above or tick rows below; nothing changes until you press Apply.
strings.preset.CurrentState.name: Current settings
strings.preset.Custom.description: Your own mix. Tick what you want on the pages below.
strings.preset.Custom.name: Custom
strings.preset.MaxPerformance.description: Privacy + Boost, plus a blank new tab and home page, a fresh start on every launch (no session restore) and a smaller disk cache. The plainest, fastest Brave.
strings.preset.MaxPerformance.name: Max Performance
strings.preset.MaxPrivacy.description: Recommended plus strict privacy: no sign-in, sync or imports, no autofill or password prompts, HTTPS only, and site data is forgotten when a tab closes. Expect signed-out sites and extra clicks.
strings.preset.MaxPrivacy.name: Max Privacy
strings.preset.Minimal.description: Switches off Brave's six loudest extras: Rewards, Wallet, VPN, Leo AI, News and Talk. Nothing else changes.
strings.preset.Minimal.name: Quick Debloat
strings.preset.None.description: Stock Brave. Nothing is ticked, so Apply removes everything this tool set and hands control back to Brave.
strings.preset.None.name: Stock / None
strings.preset.Origin.description: The free, local version of Brave Origin's idea: no Leo, Rewards, Wallet, VPN, News, Talk, Tor, Wayback Machine, Playlist, Speedreader, Email Aliases or usage analytics, with Shields kept strong.
strings.preset.Origin.name: Origin Mode
strings.preset.Performance.description: Origin Mode and Recommended together, plus Memory Saver, Battery Saver, no background running, no Cast and no Live Caption download. A lighter browser for gaming, streaming or low-power laptops.
strings.preset.Performance.name: Privacy + Boost
strings.preset.Recommended.description: Quick Debloat plus telemetry off, Chromium's AI and promo features off, and Brave's protections locked on. Passwords, autofill, sync, updates and session restore are left alone.
strings.preset.Recommended.name: Recommended
strings.result.kept: Kept {0} existing setting(s) as they were.
strings.result.restart: Fully close and reopen Brave to activate the new settings.
strings.scriptlet.affectDupes: Affect duplicate raw rules in the same file
strings.scriptlet.disabledOnly: Show disabled by this app only
strings.scriptlet.risk: Risk: disabling scriptlets can break adblocking, anti-annoyance fixes, cookie banners, video sites, or site compatibility. Brave updates may replace component versions; export disabled preferences and reapply after updates if needed.
strings.scriptlet.statusFound: Found {0} list file(s). Scanning in chunks...
strings.scriptlet.statusIdle: Scan a Brave User Data folder to list internal scriptlet rules.
strings.scriptlet.tipAffectDupes: Brave lists can contain the same scriptlet rule multiple times. Leave this on unless you only want the exact selected line.
strings.scriptlet.tipCheckFiltered: Checks every row matching the active search/show filters, including rows not currently painted in the table.
strings.searchTab.chkNtp: Override the New Tab page (writes the NewTabPageLocation policy)
strings.searchTab.chkSearch: Force this search engine (writes the DefaultSearchProvider* policies)
strings.searchTab.chkStartup: Override startup behavior (writes RestoreOnStartup and RestoreOnStartupURLs)
strings.searchTab.conflictNote: These choices win over the matching settings on the other pages (New Tab page, Home page and startup). Untick a box and press Apply to remove its override and hand control back to Brave.
strings.searchTab.searchHelp: A custom address must contain {{searchTerms}} where the query goes. Example: https://my-searx/search?q={{searchTerms}}
strings.searchTab.secStartup: On startup (what opens when you launch Brave)
strings.searchTab.startupHelp: For "specific page or set", separate several addresses with a comma. Each opens in its own tab.
strings.service.brave.description: The main background service of Brave's updater.
strings.service.brave.title: Brave Update Service
strings.service.bravem.description: The on-demand helper of Brave's updater.
strings.service.bravem.title: Brave Update Service (on demand)
strings.startupMode.specificPages: Open a specific page or set
strings.task.core.description: Brave's updater wakes up on a schedule to look for a new version. Turning it off means no automatic updates.
strings.task.core.title: Stop the updater's scheduled check
strings.task.ua.description: The scheduled task that actually checks for and downloads new Brave versions.
strings.task.ua.title: Stop the updater's version check
strings.tip.foreign: This policy already exists, but BFO did not record writing it. It stays untouched until you deliberately change this row; Apply asks before replacing or removing it.
strings.tip.hosts: Ticked groups are added to the Windows hosts file when you press Apply hosts blocks on this page. Unticked groups are removed.
strings.tip.lock: Brave already behaves this way by default. Ticking only makes it mandatory, so nothing can change it later.
strings.tip.replace: This existing policy is different from your selection. Apply shows it to you first and changes it only if you agree.
strings.tip.status: Active: already applied. Will apply / change / remove: waiting for you to press Apply. Not set: Brave decides.
strings.tip.ticked.Off: When ticked: this feature is switched off.
strings.tip.ticked.On: When ticked: this protection is kept on and locked.
strings.tip.ticked.Set: When ticked: this value is enforced and locked.
strings.tip.unticked: When unticked: Brave decides again (this tool removes its policy when you press Apply).
strings.tip.updater: Turning this off stops Brave from updating itself. Only do it if you update Brave by hand.
strings.updater.warning: Turning these off stops Brave from updating itself, so it will no longer get security fixes unless you update it by hand (Brave menu > About Brave). Only do this if you know why. Presets never touch this page.
